title: Bridge Temperature Movement
case_name: C003 - Bridge Temperature Movement (journal values, feb1bb316d08)
intro: **What it does.** Longitudinal thermal movement of the two-span FIB 36 pedestrian bridge for joint and bearing detailing: the two simple spans are treated as one continuous deck unit with the center of movement at the intermediate pier, the FDOT concrete-only temperature range (SDG Table 2.7.1-1) about a 70 °F mean, and the 120 % TU factor of SDG 2.7.1.D as a separate envelope.
overview: Longitudinal thermal movement of the two-span FIB 36 pedestrian bridge for joint and bearing detailing. The two simple spans are treated as one continuous deck unit with the center of movement at the intermediate pier; each end movement uses the adjacent span length.

The concrete-only superstructure temperature range of FDOT SDG Table 2.7.1-1 (70 °F mean, 105 °F high, 35 °F low) and the LRFD 5.4.2.2 coefficient of thermal expansion give the unfactored joint and bearing detailing movement; the FDOT SDG 2.7.1.D factor of 1.20 gives the factored TU envelope.
outside: creep, shrinkage, skew resolution and the final expansion-joint or bearing capacity checks.

L_left: The center of movement is assumed at the intermediate pier. Under this assumption, the left end movement is based on Span 1 rather than the full bridge length.
L_right: The center of movement is assumed at the intermediate pier. Under this assumption, the right end movement is based on Span 2.
L_unit: Sum the two live span lengths from Bridge Geometry_2 Beam. This total is reported for context; individual end movements are calculated from the center of movement to each end.
T_mean: The FDOT concrete-only temperature table uses a 70°F mean. Temperature values are entered numerically in degrees Fahrenheit so the thermal coefficient and temperature difference are paired consistently.
T_high: FDOT SDG Table 2.7.1-1 gives 105°F as the high temperature for a concrete-only superstructure.
T_low: FDOT SDG Table 2.7.1-1 gives 35°F as the low temperature for a concrete-only superstructure.
α_T: Use the LRFD normal-weight concrete coefficient of 6.0×10⁻⁶ per degree Fahrenheit. It is entered numerically because the temperature inputs in this module are numerical Fahrenheit values.
γ_TU: FDOT SDG 2.7.1.D directs temperature rise and fall load effects to be based on 120% of the maximum value from the temperature table. This factor is shown separately from the unfactored SDG 6.3 joint/bearing detailing movement.
ΔT_rise: Subtract the FDOT mean construction temperature from the concrete-only high temperature.
ΔT_fall: Subtract the concrete-only low temperature from the FDOT mean construction temperature.
δ_left: Multiply the concrete thermal coefficient by the FDOT temperature change and the live left-side movement length. The result is the magnitude of longitudinal movement at Begin Bridge.
δ_right: Multiply the concrete thermal coefficient by the FDOT temperature change and the live right-side movement length. The result is the magnitude of longitudinal movement at End Bridge.
δ_end_max: The longer Span 1 governs because the movement center is at the pier and thermal movement is proportional to movement length.
δ_end_to_end: Add the magnitudes at the two ends to obtain the total end-to-end change in bridge length. This is not the movement demand at a single end joint.
δ_left_TU: Apply the 1.20 temperature factor to the unfactored Begin Bridge thermal movement. This is a load-effect envelope and is kept distinct from the SDG 6.3 unfactored joint/bearing detailing movement.
δ_right_TU: Apply the 1.20 temperature factor to the unfactored End Bridge thermal movement.
δ_end_max_TU: The Begin Bridge side governs because Span 1 is slightly longer than Span 2.

working_notes: The calculation was ported from the journal module BridgeMovement (journal feb1bb316d08); every definition of the module was evaluated independently from the journal file and reproduced by the notebook to 1 part in 10⁹ before this edition was written.
